outcome.shown: A bicycle stays upright primarily through the forward motion and the forward-leaning design of its steering axis, known as the caster effect. As the bike begins to lean to one side, the geometry causes the front wheel to automatically steer into that same direction, which shifts the wheels back underneath the center of mass and restores balance. While gyroscopic effects and the mass distribution of the steering assembly contribute minor stabilizing forces, studies show that forward momentum and rider control are the essential mechanisms that keep a bicycle from falling over.
